messages.author: d28484da0c8a3f39
messages.subject: Failure with transpose matrix when defining model
parts:
Dear stan users,

I am new to stan and got a error which I am not able to solve. 

When I try to define y[j] ~ normal(mu0+lambda0[uid[j]]+gamma0[iid[j]]+ dot_product(lambda[uid[j]]’, z[iid[j]]) + dot_product(gamma[iid[j]]’, x[uid[j]]), sigsq);

It seems that I am not able to get the transpose of lambda[uid[j]] and gamma[uid[j]]. I get the error in below:



Error: unexpected ',' in:
"y[j] ~ normal(mu0+lambda0[uid[j]]+gamma0[iid[j]]+ 
dot_product(lambda[uid[j]]',"
> 
> }
Error: unexpected '}' in "}"
> '


Quotes are supposed to be the notation of transpose right? Why am I wrong here?


Any help will be appreciated. Thank you very much.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Failure with transpose matrix when defining model
parts:
The problem is that you are using a top-level ' to quote the Stan
program, so the transpose ' gets interpreted as a close string in
R. Your model's fine, at least as far as compilation goes.

You can either switch to ", in which case you won't be able to use
reject() or print() statements, or you can put the Stan program in
its own file, which is what we recommend (in person, if not yet on
our getting-started page).

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Failure with transpose matrix when defining model
parts:
Nothing jumped out at me from looking at that model, but it may also
depend on the data. Have you tried simulating data from the model and
fitting that? If a model's very missspecified, it can get stuck.

Are you getting rejection warnings during the iterations?

I'd suggest reparameterizing covariance matrices in terms of Cholesky factors.
Some of the covariance matrix transforms will be problematic in more than a
few dimensions. We should have stronger warnings in the manual about this.

The other issue to worry about is whether one parameter constrains another
parameter exactly --- that won't fly because we can't sample when there are
deterministic relations among parameters (technically the problem is that we're
sampling in K dimensions and randomizing each dimension independently, whereas
pinning one param in terms of others produces a submanifold of less than K
dimensions that we can't satisfy the constraints for with K independent jumps).

What you want to be careful of is pinning some parameter value as a function
of another variable --- that won't work in Stan and it'll cause parameters
to get stuck.

- Bob
